questions: What is the exact definition of "sum of B^p over all possible B" - is it the sum of each matrix B raised to the p-th power, or the p-th power of the sum of all matrices B?
How should the output be formatted when N=1 and the result is a single element matrix?
What is the expected behavior when p=1, given that the constraint says 1 ≤ p ≤ 10^9 but p must be prime?
How should we handle the case when there are no zeros in matrix A (K=0), meaning there is exactly one possible matrix B?
What is the precise definition of matrix exponentiation B^p in this context - standard matrix multiplication or element-wise exponentiation?
How should we interpret "modulo" in the output specification - modulo p or some other modulus?
What is the expected output format for large numbers - should they be reduced modulo p before output?
How should we handle potential integer overflow in intermediate calculations when p can be as large as 10^9?
answers: It is the sum of each matrix B raised to the p-th power, not the p-th power of the sum.
Output the single element value on its own line.
p = 1 is not prime, so it is excluded by the constraints p ≥ 2.
When K = 0, there is exactly one matrix B (the original A), so compute A^p modulo p.
Matrix exponentiation means standard repeated matrix multiplication performed modulo p.
All output elements must be reduced modulo p as specified in the problem.
Yes. Each element of the resulting matrix should be reduced modulo p individually before output.
Use modular arithmetic at each step to prevent overflow.
inline_prompts: You are given a prime number p and an N \times N matrix A = (A_{i,j}) (1\leq i,j\leq N). Each element of A is an integer between 0 and p-1, inclusive. Consider a matrix B obtained by replacing each zero in A with an integer between 1 and p-1, inclusive. There are (p-1)^K such matrices B, where K is the number of zeros in A. Find the sum of B^p over all possible B, modulo p. It is the sum of each matrix B raised to the p-th power, not the p-th power of the sum. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N p A_{1,1} \cdots A_{1,N} \vdots A_{N,1} \cdots A_{N,N} Output Print N lines. Constraints - 1 \leq N \leq 100 - p is a prime such that 1 \leq p \leq 10^9. - 0 \leq A_{i,j} \leq p-1 - All input values are integers.
